note: Fuzzer-controlled bytes are copied into an in-memory hFILE and become the input stream for htslib format detection.
The detector peeks at the attacker-controlled stream and uses the bytes to classify the file format.
The safety obligation is that a second line must exist before the code advances past the first newline; otherwise later base scanning can read past the available buffer.
A FASTA classification path calls the second-line scanner on the peeked buffer, and malformed short input can trigger the out-of-bounds read reported by ASan.
